rationale:
Split. Besides glue, the supplied proof of idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity rests on three obligations of different kinds. One is already an accepted theorem; the other two are new.
- Step 1 (frame bound 0 ≤ G ≤ 1): reuse the accepted idtp_cse_fc_planar_fibre_geometry (planar_geometry; candidate ee1e2fe5, no dependencies). Its byte-identical frozen type has exactly the parent's hypotheses (finrank Q = 2, a, e ∈ Q, unit, orthogonal). Its part (a) gives |p_T(Ax)| ≤ |πx| for every T and x, so with T = T_x, squaring and div_le_one_of_le₀ give G ≤ 1 everywhere. A new frame-bound child would only duplicate this accepted result.
- Step 2(b): a.e.-strong measurability of G for μ = R.measure (ratio_aesm, new). It follows from the accepted tangent-projection measurability, μ ≪ H^n⌞M, evaluation and division.
- Steps 4–8: a purely measure-theoretic transfer, free of IMRep (signed_transfer, new). On a finite measure space with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 a.e., suppose ∫ b H = ∫ b(φ)·ofReal(g) dν for all Borel b ≥ 0. Then H < ∞ a.e., toReal∘H is integrable, the signed identity holds for bounded Borel b, and ∫_S H = ∫_{φ⁻¹S} ofReal(g) dν.
ratio_aesm needs the accepted imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm, which the selected node already lists as its dependency. Sibling dependencies must name keys of this decomposition, and the proof base (pristine dispatch commit d9c9559b) lacks that theorem. So it is listed as the reused child tangent_aesm with its byte-identical type (accepted, candidate 36b2d372), as the flux_density decomposition did.
The two reused children create no new node or work. Dependencies: ratio_aesm→tangent_aesm only, so the graph is acyclic. The two new children are leaves at depth 6, the maximum (about 15 and 67 lines of Lean).
Other accepted results were checked and rejected. idtp_cse_bml_tilt_pointwise_bound states G ≤ 1 but needs radial tangency, which is unavailable here. codim1_ac_pp_setIntegral_transfer quantifies over all, not only Borel, test functions. dorag_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm would only replace one line of ratio_aesm.

Parent assembly after the split (glue only, about 61 lines of Lean):
1. F̃ = (|·|, arctan(⟨·,e⟩/⟨·,a⟩)) is measurable (measurable_norm.prodMk, Real.continuous_arctan.measurable, Measurable.div), and Sq(s') is Borel.
2. Z ⊆ closedBall(0, 1+|s|), since |x| − 1 < s ≤ |s|. Also μ(closedBall) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH² ≠ ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence (μ⌞Z)(univ) = μ(Z) ≠ ∞.
3. ratio_aesm (n = 2, U = univ).restrict gives a.e.-strong measurability of G for μ⌞Z.
4. 0 ≤ G by positivity, and G ≤ 1 everywhere from planar_geometry (a) with T = T_x. ae_of_all makes this μ⌞Z-a.e. No measurability of Z is needed.
5. Apply signed_transfer with X = ℝ^P, ν = μ⌞Z, φ = F̃ and g = G. Its identity hypothesis is literally the given one, because a set integral is the integral for the restricted measure. Its first three conclusions are (i)–(iii) verbatim.
6. (iv): for s' ≤ s, the set conclusion with S = Sq(s') and Measure.restrict_restrict (F̃⁻¹(Sq) is measurable) give ∫_{Sq} H = ∫_{F̃⁻¹(Sq) ∩ Z} ofReal(G) dμ. Moreover F̃⁻¹(Sq) ∩ Z(s,s) = Z(s,s'), by abs_sub_lt_iff, abs_lt and s' ≤ s; the last condition keeps s.

subproblems.title: The approximate tangent plane field of an integer multiplicity triple is measurable
subproblems.statement: For every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in a set U ⊆ ℝ^P (IMRep U n), the map x ↦ p_{T_xM}, the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x (the approximate tangent plane T_xM where it exists, {0} otherwise), is H^n⌞M-almost everywhere strongly measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.tangent_projection_measurable-a1, status accepted with candidate commit 36b2d372), reused here by Lean name with its byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new node and no new proof work is created. The selected node idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity already lists that node as its dependency; listing it as a child lets the sibling ratio_aesm declare it as a dependency, so the controller overlays its accepted history into that sibling, whose frozen proof base (the pristine dispatch commit d9c9559b) does not contain it. In the present decomposition it supplies the H^n⌞M-a.e. strong measurability of x ↦ p_{T_x} used in step 1 of the proof of ratio_aesm (step 2(b) of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity). The numbered proof below is the one reviewed and accepted for that node, reproduced verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 3 §1 (T_xM is unique, 1.5(1)) and the definition 6.3.1 of an integer multiplicity current, in which ξ orients T_xM in an H^n-measurable way; this measurability is implicit in Simon's formulas ∫ div_M X dμ_V (Ch. 4, 2.2–2.7) used in steps 2, 5 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. a.e. identification. Let μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. At such x the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so approxTangentPlane n M x is some Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'; by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) Q' = Q_x.
2. Case n = 0. Every Q with finrank 0 equals ⊥, and approxTangentPlane 0 M x is ⊥ in both branches of its definition, so the map is the constant 0, which is strongly measurable. Assume n ≥ 1.
3. A unit simple n-vector determines its plane. Let ζ ∈ (Λ^n)^* with ζ(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, τ orthonormal, s = ±1. Claim: span τ = {v : ζ(ι_vβ) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector β}, where ι_vβ(u_1, …, u_n) := β(v, u_1, …, u_n). If v ∈ span τ then β(v, τ_1, …, τ_n) = 0 because the arguments are linearly dependent. If v ∉ span τ, let w := v − Σ_i⟨v, τ_i⟩τ_i ≠ 0 and β(u_0, …, u_n) := det(⟨c_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b=0..n} with c := (w, τ_1, …, τ_n), a continuous alternating (n+1)-form; the matrix (⟨c_a, (v, τ_1, …, τ_n)_b⟩) has first row (|w|², 0, …, 0) and lower-right block I_n, so β(v, τ) = |w|² and ζ(ι_vβ) = s|w|² ≠ 0. Consequently, if ζ orients both Q and Q' (IsUnitOrientationOf) then Q = Q'.
4. Continuity of the orientation-to-projection map. Let Ω := {(τ, s) : τ ∈ (ℝ^P)^n orthonormal, s ∈ {1, −1}}, a compact set, and Φ(τ, s) := (β ↦ s·β(τ)), a continuous map Ω → (Λ^n)^* (multilinear evaluation with |τ_i| = 1). Its image 𝒮 is compact, hence closed, and equals the set of ζ for which ∃ Q, IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. The map G̃(τ, s) := Σ_i ⟨τ_i, ·⟩τ_i = starProjection(span τ) is continuous on Ω and, by step 3, constant on the fibres of Φ; hence G̃ = G∘Φ for a unique G : 𝒮 → End(ℝ^P). Since Φ : Ω → 𝒮 is a continuous surjection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space, it is a quotient map, so G is continuous on 𝒮. Extend G by 0 outside 𝒮; the extension is Borel measurable (𝒮 closed, G continuous on it).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x (step 1), ξ(x) = Φ(τ, s) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q_x = approxTangentPlane n M x, hence starProjection(approxTangentPlane n M x) = G(ξ(x)). Since ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and G is Borel, G∘ξ is μ-a.e. measurable; End(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional (second countable and metrizable), so G∘ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so is the μ-a.e. equal map x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection.

(Clarification of references inside the reproduced proof, not a change of argument: "steps 2, 5 and 6 of the parent proof" refer to the original parent of that accepted node, DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1; in the present decomposition the theorem is used only through its stated conclusion, the H^n⌞M-a.e. strong measurability of x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection.)
proof_key_steps: Almost everywhere the approximate tangent plane is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (uniqueness of T_xM).
A unit simple n-vector determines its plane (kernel of v ↦ ζ(ι_v ·)).
The map unit simple n-vector ↦ projection is continuous on the compact set of such vectors (quotient-map argument); compose with the a.e.-measurable ξ.

subproblems.title: Planar fibre geometry: projection formula, the sector point and uniqueness of the planar fibre point
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P (Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2) and a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0. Write π := Q.starProjection (orthogonal projection onto Q), p_T := T.starProjection for a linear subspace T, Ax := ⟨x, a⟩e − ⟨x, e⟩a and f(x) := arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩). Then (a) |p_T(Ax)| ≤ |πx| ≤ |x| for every linear subspace T ⊆ ℝ^P and every x ∈ ℝ^P; and for all real t > 0 and α with |α| < Real.pi/2 (Real.pi is the circle constant; π denotes the projection), the point x₀ := t(cos α·a + sin α·e) satisfies (b) ⟨x₀, a⟩ > 0, |x₀| = t, f(x₀) = α, πx₀ = x₀ and |π(Ax₀)| = t, and (c) every x ∈ ℝ^P with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, |x| = t, f(x) = α and x ≠ x₀ satisfies |πx| < t.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → (∀ (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P), ‖T.starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a)‖ ≤ ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ∧ ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ≤ ‖x‖) ∧ ∀ t α : ℝ, 0 < t → |α| < Real.pi / 2 → (0 < inner ℝ (t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)) a ∧ ‖t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)‖ = t ∧ Real.arctan (inner ℝ (t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)) e / inner ℝ (t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)) a) = α ∧ Q.starProjection (t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)) = t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e) ∧ ‖Q.starProjection (inner ℝ (t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)) a • e - inner ℝ (t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e)) e • a)‖ = t) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid P, 0 < inner ℝ x a → ‖x‖ = t → Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a) = α → x ≠ t • (Real.cos α • a + Real.sin α • e) → ‖Q.starProjection x‖ < t
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem idtp_cse_fc_planar_fibre_geometry (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.integer_density_tangent_planes-a1.cone_sector_endpoint_density-a1.fibre_count-a1.planar_geometry-a1, status accepted with candidate commit ee1e2fe5, no dependencies), reused here by Lean name with its byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new node and no new proof work is created. Listing it as a child makes the controller overlay its accepted history into the proof base of the selected node idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity (the pristine dispatch commit d9c9559b does not contain it). In the present decomposition only its part (a) is used: |p_T(Ax)| ≤ |πx| for every subspace T and every x. With T = T_x it gives G(x) ≤ 1 for every x by squaring and div_le_one_of_le₀ (also when πx = 0, since t/0 = 0), while G(x) ≥ 0 holds because G is a quotient of squares. This supplies step 1 (frame bound) of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity, whose hypotheses dim Q = 2, a, e ∈ Q, |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0 are exactly the hypotheses of this theorem. The numbered proof below is the one reviewed and accepted for that node, reproduced verbatim.

Source: parent conventions (F1)–(F3) and step 1(i)–(iii), specialized. Notation: π := Q.starProjection; for a subspace T, p_T := T.starProjection; Ax := ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a; f(x) := arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩); x₀ := t(cos α·a + sin α·e). Facts used about orthogonal projections onto a subspace K: |p_K v| ≤ |v| (`Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le`); p_K v = v iff v ∈ K (`Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff`); |p_K v| = |v| iff v ∈ K (`Submodule.mem_iff_norm_starProjection`); if y ∈ K and ⟨v − y, w⟩ = 0 for all w ∈ K then p_K v = y (`Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero`).
1. (Gram matrix.) ⟨e,a⟩ = ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, ⟨a,a⟩ = |a|² = 1 and ⟨e,e⟩ = |e|² = 1. Hence the family (a, e) is orthonormal, in particular linearly independent.
2. (Q = span{a, e}.) span{a, e} ⊆ Q since a, e ∈ Q, and dim span{a, e} = 2 by step 1 (`finrank_span_eq_card`), which equals dim Q. A subspace contained in a finite-dimensional subspace of the same dimension equals it (`Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq`), so Q = span{a, e}: every w ∈ Q has the form c₁a + c₂e (`Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun`).
3. (Projection formula.) Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and put y := ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e ∈ Q. By step 1, ⟨x − y, a⟩ = ⟨x,a⟩ − ⟨x,a⟩·1 − ⟨x,e⟩·0 = 0 and ⟨x − y, e⟩ = ⟨x,e⟩ − ⟨x,a⟩·0 − ⟨x,e⟩·1 = 0, so ⟨x − y, c₁a + c₂e⟩ = 0 for all c₁, c₂, i.e. x − y is orthogonal to every w ∈ Q (step 2). By the characterization of the orthogonal projection, πx = ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e.
4. (Norm identities.) For u, v ∈ ℝ, expanding the inner products with step 1: |u e − v a|² = u²⟨e,e⟩ − 2uv⟨e,a⟩ + v²⟨a,a⟩ = u² + v², and |u a + v e|² = u²⟨a,a⟩ + 2uv⟨a,e⟩ + v²⟨e,e⟩ = u² + v². With u = ⟨x,a⟩, v = ⟨x,e⟩ and step 3 this gives |Ax|² = |πx|², hence |Ax| = |πx| (both are nonnegative).
5. (Part (a).) For every subspace T and every x: |p_T(Ax)| ≤ |Ax| = |πx| by step 4, and |πx| ≤ |x|.
6. (Part (b).) Let t > 0 and |α| < Real.pi/2. Then −Real.pi/2 < α < Real.pi/2, so cos α > 0. By step 1, ⟨x₀,a⟩ = t(cos α⟨a,a⟩ + sin α⟨e,a⟩) = t cos α > 0 and ⟨x₀,e⟩ = t(cos α⟨a,e⟩ + sin α⟨e,e⟩) = t sin α. By step 4 with (u, v) = (cos α, sin α), |cos α·a + sin α·e|² = cos²α + sin²α = 1, so |x₀| = |t|·1 = t. Next ⟨x₀,e⟩/⟨x₀,a⟩ = (t sin α)/(t cos α) = sin α/cos α = tan α, and arctan(tan α) = α because −Real.pi/2 < α < Real.pi/2 (`Real.arctan_tan`); thus f(x₀) = α. Since a, e ∈ Q, x₀ ∈ Q and therefore πx₀ = x₀. Finally Ax₀ = ⟨x₀,a⟩e − ⟨x₀,e⟩a ∈ Q, so π(Ax₀) = Ax₀ and |π(Ax₀)| = |Ax₀| = |πx₀| = |x₀| = t by step 4.
7. (Part (c): reduction to Q.) Let t, α be as in step 6 and let x satisfy ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, |x| = t, f(x) = α and x ≠ x₀. Suppose, for contradiction, that |πx| ≥ t. Since |πx| ≤ |x| = t, we get |πx| = |x|, hence x ∈ Q and x = πx. Put u := ⟨x,a⟩ > 0 and v := ⟨x,e⟩. By step 3, x = u a + v e, and by step 4, u² + v² = |πx|² = |x|² = t².
8. (Part (c): the angle.) Here α = f(x) = arctan(v/u). Since 1 + (v/u)² = (u² + v²)/u² = (t/u)² and t/u > 0, we have √(1 + (v/u)²) = t/u. Using cos(arctan z) = 1/√(1 + z²) and sin(arctan z) = z/√(1 + z²) (`Real.cos_arctan`, `Real.sin_arctan`): cos α = u/t and sin α = (v/u)·(u/t) = v/t. Therefore x₀ = t(cos α·a + sin α·e) = u a + v e = x, contradicting x ≠ x₀. Hence |πx| < t. ∎

(Clarification of references inside the reproduced proof, not a change of argument: "parent conventions (F1)–(F3) and step 1(i)–(iii)" refer to the original parent of that accepted node, DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.integer_density_tangent_planes-a1.cone_sector_endpoint_density-a1.fibre_count-a1; in the present decomposition the theorem is used only through its stated conclusion (a).)
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is orthonormal and a dimension count gives Q = span{a, e}.
πx = ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e by the orthogonality characterization of the projection.
For x₀ = t(cos α a + sin α e): ⟨x₀,a⟩ = t cos α > 0, |x₀| = t, f(x₀) = arctan(tan α) = α, x₀ ∈ Q and |π(Ax₀)| = |Ax₀| = t.
If |πx| = |x| = t then x = ua + ve ∈ Q with u > 0 and u² + v² = t²; cos α = u/t and sin α = v/t force x = x₀.

subproblems.title: A.e. strong measurability of the tangential rotation ratio for the weight of an integer multiplicity triple
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with weight μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ (H^n = μHE[n]), Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π = Q.starProjection, and a, e ∈ ℝ^P. Put T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x with orthogonal projection p_{T_x}, Ax := ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a and G(x) := |p_{T_x}(Ax)|² / |πx|² (real division, t/0 = 0). Then G : ℝ^P → ℝ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x : Euclid P => ‖(approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a)‖ ^ 2 / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2) R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(b) (measurability of G) of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity, stated for general n and U and for the unrestricted weight μ (the parent then restricts to its sector Z).
1. (Tangent projection field.) By the accepted sibling theorem tangent_aesm, i.e. Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm applied to P, n, U and R, the operator-valued map x ↦ p_{T_x} = (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection, with values in ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ^P, is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier.
2. (Transfer to μ.) By definition (IMRep.measure), μ = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, so μ ≪ H^n⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). A.e. strong measurability passes to an absolutely continuous measure (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac), so x ↦ p_{T_x} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
3. (Evaluation at Ax.) The map x ↦ Ax = ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a is continuous (continuity of the inner product, of scalar multiplication and of subtraction), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable. The evaluation (L, v) ↦ L v is the continuous bilinear map given by the identity continuous linear map of the operator space ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ^P. Applying ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ to it, to the map of step 2 and to x ↦ Ax shows that x ↦ p_{T_x}(Ax) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
4. (Numerator.) Norm and squaring are continuous, so N(x) := |p_{T_x}(Ax)|² is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and in particular μ-a.e. measurable as a real-valued function.
5. (Denominator.) D(x) := |πx|² is continuous (π is a continuous linear map; norm and squaring are continuous), hence measurable.
6. (Quotient.) Real division is a measurable operation on ℝ (ℝ has measurable division in both arguments, including the convention t/0 = 0), so G = N/D is μ-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.div). As ℝ is second countable and metrizable, a μ-a.e. measurable real-valued function is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable). Hence G is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: tangent_aesm: x ↦ p_{T_x} is H^n⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; μ = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ H^n⌞M transfers this to μ (mono_ac).
Evaluation at the continuous field Ax (aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ with the identity of the operator space), then norm and square.
Divide by the continuous |πx|² (AEMeasurable.div) and convert back to a.e. strong measurability.

subproblems.title: From a nonnegative pushforward-density identity on a finite measure space to finiteness, integrability, signed and set identities
subproblems.statement: Let X be a measurable space with a measure ν such that ν(X) < ∞, φ : X → ℝ² a measurable map, g : X → ℝ a ν-a.e. strongly measurable function with 0 ≤ g(x) ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x, and H : ℝ² → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ² = ℝ × ℝ, such that ∫ b(p)H(p) dp = ∫ b(φ(x))·ofReal(g(x)) dν(x) for every Borel b : ℝ² → [0,∞] (lower integrals). Then (i) H(p) ≠ ∞ for a.e. p; (ii) toReal∘H is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ²; (iii) for every Borel b : ℝ² → ℝ with |b| ≤ M for some real M, ∫ b(p)·toReal(H(p)) dp = ∫ b(φ(x))·g(x) dν(x) (Bochner integrals); (iv) for every Borel S ⊆ ℝ², ∫_S H(p) dp = ∫_{φ⁻¹(S)} ofReal(g(x)) dν(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (φ : X → ℝ × ℝ) (g : X → ℝ) (H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), ν univ ≠ ∞ → Measurable φ → AEStronglyMeasurable g ν → (∀ᵐ x ∂ν, 0 ≤ g x ∧ g x ≤ 1) → AEMeasurable H volume → (∀ b : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable b → ∫⁻ p : ℝ × ℝ, b p * H p = ∫⁻ x, b (φ x) * ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂ν) → (∀ᵐ p : ℝ × ℝ, H p ≠ ∞) ∧ Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => (H p).toReal) ∧ (∀ b : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, Measurable b → (∃ M : ℝ, ∀ p, |b p| ≤ M) → ∫ p : ℝ × ℝ, b p * (H p).toReal = ∫ x, b (φ x) * g x ∂ν) ∧ ∀ S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), MeasurableSet S → ∫⁻ p in S, H p = ∫⁻ x in φ ⁻¹' S, ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂ν
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–8 of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_fd_fibre_signed_identity (finiteness, integrability, nonnegative and signed identities, indicator identity), abstracted from the specific triple, sector and map: there ν = μ⌞Z, φ = F̃ = (|·|, f), g = G, and the only properties used are ν(X) = μ(Z) < ∞ (parent step 3), 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 (parent step 1, supplied in this decomposition by the reused sibling planar_geometry), measurability of F̃ and a.e. strong measurability of G for μ⌞Z (parent step 2, supplied by the sibling ratio_aesm). Notation: H_ℝ := toReal∘H, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, toReal = ENNReal.toReal, dp = Lebesgue measure on ℝ² (volume on ℝ × ℝ), Borel = measurable.
1. (Finite mass.) ν is a finite measure because ν(X) < ∞. The constant function 1 is Borel, so the hypothesis with b ≡ 1 gives ∫ H dp = ∫ ofReal(g) dν. For ν-a.e. x, g(x) ≤ 1 and hence ofReal(g(x)) ≤ 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_one), so lintegral_mono_ae gives ∫ ofReal(g) dν ≤ ∫ 1 dν = ν(X) < ∞. Hence ∫ H dp < ∞.
2. ((i).) H is a.e.-measurable with finite lower integral (step 1), so H(p) < ∞, i.e. H(p) ≠ ∞, for a.e. p (ae_lt_top').
3. ((ii).) H is a.e.-measurable and ∫ H dp ≠ ∞, so H_ℝ = toReal∘H is integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top; equivalently: H_ℝ is a.e.-strongly measurable by AEMeasurable.ennreal_toReal, nonnegative, and ∫ ofReal(H_ℝ) dp ≤ ∫ H dp < ∞ by ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le, so it has finite integral by hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal). Moreover, by step 2, ofReal(H_ℝ(p)) = H(p) for a.e. p (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
4. (Nonnegative bounded test functions.) Let β : ℝ² → ℝ be Borel with 0 ≤ β(p) ≤ M for all p.
(a) p ↦ β(p)H_ℝ(p) is integrable, since β is measurable with |β| ≤ M and H_ℝ is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul); it is nonnegative. The map x ↦ β(φ(x))g(x) is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (β∘φ is measurable as a composition of measurable maps; product with the ν-a.e. strongly measurable g), and for ν-a.e. x we have 0 ≤ β(φ(x))g(x) ≤ M·1 = M (from 0 ≤ β ≤ M and 0 ≤ g(x) ≤ 1); hence it is integrable for the finite measure ν (Integrable.of_bound) and ν-a.e. nonnegative.
(b) By integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, ∫ β(p)H_ℝ(p) dp = toReal(∫ ofReal(β(p)H_ℝ(p)) dp) and ∫ β(φ(x))g(x) dν = toReal(∫ ofReal(β(φ(x))g(x)) dν).
(c) For a.e. p, ofReal(β(p)H_ℝ(p)) = ofReal(β(p))·ofReal(H_ℝ(p)) = ofReal(β(p))·H(p) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, since β(p) ≥ 0, and step 3); hence ∫ ofReal(βH_ℝ) dp = ∫ ofReal(β(p))·H(p) dp (lintegral_congr_ae). For every x, ofReal(β(φ(x))g(x)) = ofReal(β(φ(x)))·ofReal(g(x)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, since β(φ(x)) ≥ 0). The function b := ofReal∘β : ℝ² → [0,∞] is Borel (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal composed with β), so the hypothesis gives ∫ ofReal(β(p))·H(p) dp = ∫ ofReal(β(φ(x)))·ofReal(g(x)) dν. Therefore the two lower integrals in (b) are equal, and ∫ βH_ℝ dp = ∫ β(φ)g dν.
5. ((iii).) Let b : ℝ² → ℝ be Borel with |b(p)| ≤ M for all p; then M ≥ |b(0,0)| ≥ 0. Put b⁺ := max(b, 0) and b⁻ := max(−b, 0). They are Borel, take values in [0, M] (because b ≤ |b| ≤ M, −b ≤ |b| ≤ M and M ≥ 0), and b = b⁺ − b⁻ pointwise (max_zero_sub_eq_self). Hence, pointwise, b·H_ℝ = b⁺H_ℝ − b⁻H_ℝ and (b∘φ)·g = (b⁺∘φ)g − (b⁻∘φ)g (sub_mul), and the four functions on the right are integrable by step 4(a) applied to β = b⁺ and β = b⁻. By integral_sub and step 4(c): ∫ bH_ℝ dp = ∫ b⁺H_ℝ dp − ∫ b⁻H_ℝ dp = ∫ b⁺(φ)g dν − ∫ b⁻(φ)g dν = ∫ b(φ)g dν.
6. ((iv).) Let S ⊆ ℝ² be Borel and b := 1_S, the indicator of S with value 1; it is Borel (measurable_one.indicator). On the left, 1_S(p)·H(p) equals the indicator of S applied to H at p (check p ∈ S and p ∉ S separately), so ∫ 1_S(p)H(p) dp = ∫_S H dp (lintegral_indicator, S measurable). On the right, 1_S(φ(x))·ofReal(g(x)) equals the indicator of φ⁻¹(S) applied to ofReal∘g at x (check φ(x) ∈ S and φ(x) ∉ S separately), and φ⁻¹(S) is measurable because φ is; so ∫ 1_S(φ(x))·ofReal(g(x)) dν = ∫_{φ⁻¹(S)} ofReal(g) dν (lintegral_indicator). The hypothesis with b = 1_S equates the two left-hand sides, which proves (iv). ∎
proof_key_steps: b ≡ 1 and 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 a.e. give ∫ H ≤ ν(X) < ∞, hence H < ∞ a.e. (ae_lt_top') and toReal∘H integrable.

For Borel 0 ≤ β ≤ M both sides are integrable nonnegative functions; their lower integrals agree by the hypothesis with b = ofReal∘β and ofReal_mul, so the Bochner integrals agree (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae).
A bounded signed b splits as max(b,0) − max(−b,0); integral_sub gives (iii).
b = 1_S with lintegral_indicator on both sides gives (iv).
